scope.flow: Cross-chain unstake on spoke chain: UnstakeMessenger.unstake() with buffered-fee helper quoting, calling _lzSend/_payNative on the LayerZero endpoint
scope.environment: LayerZero OAppSender-based cross-chain unstake messenger (UnstakeMessenger) with buffered-fee quote helpers

statements.text: UnstakeMessenger.unstake(uint256 returnTripAllocation) is the cross-chain unstake entrypoint on the spoke chain and encodes msg.sender as the user.
The buffered-fee helper quoteUnstakeWithBuffer() deliberately returns a fee larger than the exact LayerZero quote (for example, exactFee * 110 / 100).
unstake() enforces msg.value >= fee.nativeFee, reverting with InsufficientFee if the caller underpays.
unstake() calls _lzSend(hubEid, payload, options, fee, payable(msg.sender)) passing the exact quoted fee struct to the LayerZero endpoint.
The inherited LayerZero OAppSender._payNative() implementation requires msg.value to equal the native fee exactly.
When the integrator follows the buffered-fee pattern, the caller sends unstake{value: bufferedFee}(returnTripAllocation), so msg.value exceeds the exact quoted fee.nativeFee.
Caller calls unstake{value: bufferedFee}(returnTripAllocation) with the buffered fee from quoteUnstakeWithBuffer().
unstake() invokes _lzSend() which calls _payNative(), observing msg.value against the passed fee.nativeFee.
unstake() passes the exact quoted fee.nativeFee to _lzSend while _payNative() enforces strict equality, so any msg.value above the exact quote makes _payNative() observe a mismatch and revert.
Unstake calls revert with OAppSender.NotEnoughNative(uint256) when msg.value equals the bufferedFee that is 10% higher than exactFee.
Unstake reverts even when msg.value equals exactFee + 1 wei, before any LayerZero message is dispatched.
The buffered-fee integration pattern exposed by the contract is unusable in practice, so users cannot complete cross-chain unstake operations via the buffered flow.

The UnstakeMessenger.unstake() operation should complete when the caller supplies the buffered fee returned by quoteUnstakeWithBuffer() (at least the exact quoted native fee), rather than reverting on a msg.value above the exact quote. (Inferred from the report's claim that the buffered-fee integration pattern is intended to be usable.)
The buffered-fee helper flow (quote buffer, then forward that value as msg.value, with excess refunded) is the intended supported integration pattern whose failure constitutes the issue.

ambiguities: No explicit authorization/permission clause is stated for who may call unstake(); the report only says callers/integrators use the helper.
The report does not establish whether a real on-chain buffered-fee unstake transaction occurred; revert behavior is described via tests and conditional reasoning.
The report does not specify the hubEid/chain or the exact payload/options values used.
Refund behavior for excess value on a successful path is mentioned as a design intent but not established as a verified state change.
